full_judgment: 42. We further hold the view that the expression "wide circulation" as occurring in section 138 does not require that the news paper must have any particular number of issues. The term "wide circulation" is not defined by the NI Act. So, keeping in view of the legislative intent with regard to knowledge of the drawer of he cheque, a newspaper can be considered as having "wide circulation" if it is regularly published and it has a sufficient network for ensuring the availability thereof to the readers of the locality of the drawer. The legislative presumption is that the drawer would somehow gather knowledge of the notice either by himself or from others of the locality.
